comparison:
Independent A2 decisions agree with all 50 pack predicates. This is agreement about the selected texts’ stance, not verification of the propositions’ truth or of unsampled records. The audit already reclassified Kambhampati, Chalmers and Mahowald as context; the independent checks agree. Omohundro’s 2008 revision and Davis’s October 2014 manuscript also agree with the hidden dates.

A1 produced earlier leads for R03 (2016 migrated page, still historically unpinned), R04 (Corrigibility, January 2015), R05 (CFAI, 2001 version date in later reflow), R06 (Goertzel, May 2002), R07 (Joy, April 2000), R10a (Goertzel, February 2004), R10b (Yudkowsky introductory essay, May 2001), and R14 (Marcus and Davis, September 2019). These vary in certainty: the 2016 daemon page and 2001 reflow require historical-byte authentication; the R06 and R10b criterion fits merit adjudication. The independent R16 selection was later than Brooks 2017 and is not an improvement on the pack. Existing B1/A4 overlap decisions mean an earlier R04/R05 passage may call for a cross-link rather than a duplicate record.

Postblind archive retrieval adds stronger results: Bostrom’s arbitrary-goal and days-rather-than-years wording is present by 6 August 2003, even though the original proceedings were not obtained. Crawford’s 25 June 2016 essay explicitly prioritizes documented discrimination over existential-threat discussion, predating DAIR 2023 on R12. These change the evidence behind the audit’s earliest-located conclusions. Preserve capture dates separately from publication dates.

Keep Bostrom 2002 on R09: the government’s selected restrictive future, human control of the superintelligence and deliberate goal selection meet power entrenchment and irreversible catastrophe conditionally. No claim of mass casualties, motive or realized use is needed.

Part B requires two proposed stance changes: item 92 (Andreessen on R10b) to bears on, because present control/ownership is not a design mechanism; item 96 (Brooks on R01) to bears on, because understanding harm does not entail concern for humans. Item 90’s ≤1-year summary is a borderline fit under the strict R05 timescale; cite a qualifying whole-transition passage or settle the boundary explicitly. Item 82 should retain the model-free value-instilling caveat, in addition to value choice.

Dates/locators: item 87 currently displays 31 August 2022, despite the brief’s October 14 date and the audit’s statement that the byline was corrected. Item 95 displays both October 25 and October 26. Item 100 uses a publication date while acknowledging 2020 modification. Goertzel’s page has conflicting month/issue labels. Item 38’s November 2015 is supported by file creation metadata, not a verified publication date. Item 106’s list is section 2; item 117’s cascading-boom passage is point 4. Item 94’s reference to a 2023 copy of a 2024 essay needs correction.

Archive comparisons resolve the sampled Bengio-date concerns and establish 2014 response attestations for Edge, without making current page order a publication chronology. The report retains the original item answers and adds these resolutions visibly.

All four missing seeds were retrieved from dated captures. Only qualifying balance additions are proposed: Violet Hour 2024 on R03; Arctotherium 2026 on R17; Corrigibility 2015 on R10a and R10b; Hadshar 2023 on R11; Encode Justice–FLI 2023 on R12; Davidson 2023 on R05 through the explicit fast-takeoff naming route, with its distinct automation metric stated. No additional broad R09 counter-text was selected. Full-pack membership was checked only after blind commitment; these texts were not found among its documents or source URLs.

Outstanding evidential limits: original Bostrom 2003 proceedings pages remain uninspected; CFAI’s 2001 wording and the daemon page’s 2016 wording remain unpinned historical leads. No source retrieval failure is treated as a negative historical finding. Maintainer/admission work should adjudicate the proposed classifications and historical roles; this report changes neither data nor the pack.
